newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWEDISH NEWSPRINT PRICES TO BE CUT 10 PCT - PRINTER.
newsitem.headline: SWEDISH NEWSPRINT PRICES TO BE CUT 10 PCT - PRINTER.

text.p: Newspaper Printers, the group responsible for printing two of Sweden's major daily newspapers, on Monday said it had reached an agreement for newsprint prices to be cut by 10 percent from January.
"The agreement means a lowering of newsprint prices by 10 percent compared with the last agreement in the autumn," Newspaper Printers' managing director Thomas Salzman told Reuters.
The agreement was reached last week with forestry companies MoDo , SCA and Stora and will stand for deliveries throughout 1997.

This means that the price of news print in Sweden will be lower than the rest of Europe, according to Salzman whose company prints daily broadsheet Svenska Dagbladet and afternoon tabloid Aftonbladet.
"I do not think that prices will be cut further in 1997," he said.
Salzman said lower newsprint prices were necessary for many buyers.

"Most Swedish newspapers are under a lot of pressure. Paper prices have risen 40 percent in the last two years which really had an effect in 1996. A price cut is a question of survival for many newspapers in the sector," Salzman said.
